chapters.title: Hook
lines: Your laptop's on the TV. Or the projector. Or across the room.
This is Edgepad version four. An open-source Android app that turns your phone into a control deck for your laptop.

chapters.title: The surface
lines: A multi-touch trackpad with remappable gestures.
Corner dials for volume, brightness, zoom and scrubbing. Flip one switch, and four become eight.

chapters.title: Controls
lines: A full keyboard. A gamepad your laptop sees as a real Xbox controller, on Windows and Linux.
A pen that draws on your screen. Screenshots and recordings, saved to your phone.
Macros for apps, URLs and scripts. Clipboard sync, both ways.

chapters.title: Everywhere
lines: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or USB. Windows, Mac and Linux. Mac, Linux, Wi-Fi and USB are new and in beta.
No account. No server. No cloud. Every line of code is public.

chapters.title: Get it
lines: Edgepad. Free and open source, on GitHub.
Your laptop, from anywhere in the room.
